tagline: An AI generation tool sold as a hosted subscription, in the now-standard model-wrapper shape.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: We have not verified this product's exact feature set, so treat this entry as a shape judgment rather than a teardown. Products in this class are thin, well-designed layers over foundation models you can rent yourself with an API key, which means the generation quality is not the seller's asset. What you are paying for is a prompt library someone else tuned, a UI that does not make you think, and the fact that the billing and the rate limits are somebody else's problem. A coding agent can reproduce the core loop in a session: pick a model provider, wrap it in prompt templates, store the outputs. The gaps show up in the parts nobody screenshots: usage caps, retries, cost control, mobile, and whatever the hosted version quietly does to clean up model output before you see it.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app with saved prompt templates that sends your inputs to a hosted model API and keeps every result in a searchable history.
requirements: An API key for a hosted model provider (OpenAI, Anthropic, or similar)
Willingness to pay per-token instead of per-month
whatYouLose: Prompt engineering someone else already iterated on with real users
Predictable flat billing instead of a metered API bill that can surprise you
Any mobile or tablet experience worth using
Guardrails and output cleanup that hide the model's rougher edges
Someone else swapping in the newer, better model for you
moatNotes: When the model is rented, the only defensible parts are taste and the fact that the customer never sees a token counter.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because renting the model is the easy half. The hard half is knowing which prompt actually produces the output you wanted, and a paid tool has already burned through that trial and error on other people's behalf. Flat monthly pricing also feels safer than a metered API key, even when it is more expensive, because nobody wants to audit their own usage. If you use this kind of tool twice a month, a subscription is silly. If you use it daily and the output feeds real work, the polish is doing more than you think.
notes: Graded as a category, not as a specific product, because the specifics are unverified.
prompt:
Build a local-first AI generation workspace. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, non-negotiable:
- Next.js with the App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/app.db
- One model provider: OpenAI-compatible chat completions, base URL and key from .env

Env:
- Create .env.example with OPENAI_API_KEY, OPENAI_BASE_URL, MODEL_NAME
- Never commit .env, never hardcode a key, never log the key

Features in scope:
1. Template library: create, edit, delete named prompt templates with {{variable}} placeholders. Store in SQLite.
2. Run view: pick a template, fill in its variables in a generated form, submit, stream the response token by token into the page.
3. History: every run saved with template id, filled inputs, full output, model name, token counts if the API returns them, timestamp. Full text search over outputs.
4. Rerun: open any history row, tweak the inputs, run again as a new row.
5. Cost meter: a running total of tokens used this month, with a configurable per-1k-token rate in settings so the number means something.
6. Export: dump all templates and history to a single JSON file, and import it back.

Out of scope, do not build:
- Auth, multi-user, billing, sharing links, mobile app, image or video generation, background jobs

Quality bar:
- Handle API errors and rate limits with a visible retry, do not swallow them
- Seed the DB with three example templates on first run
- README with setup in under ten lines and one npm run dev to start
